name: Strozzi NoSQL
tagline: Carlo Strozzi's 1998 shell-based relational database of plain-text tables and Unix pipe operators.
description: Strozzi NoSQL is a relational database management system made of small Unix operators that read and write tab-separated ASCII tables, so a query is a shell pipeline: select rows, join tables, sort and report by chaining commands, and edit or version data with ordinary tools like vi, diff or RCS. It descends from the RDB system written at RAND and follows the operator-stream paradigm described in Unix Review in 1991. Carlo Strozzi has distributed it under the GPL since 1998, and its name, which simply means it does not use SQL, predates the 2009 NoSQL movement it has nothing to do with. The last release, 4.1.11, came out in 2014.
statusNote: Still downloadable from strozzi.it, but the last release was 4.1.11 (June 2014) and the project is dormant.
strengths: Tables are plain text, so grep, diff, editors and version control work on the data directly
Queries compose like any Unix pipeline, easy to script
Tiny, transparent and dependency-light on Linux
weaknesses: No transactions, concurrency control or SQL
Performance limited by text parsing and process pipelines
Dormant since 2014 with a very small user base
Name collides with the unrelated NoSQL movement, confusing searches
useCases: Small scripted data jobs on Unix
Teaching the relational model with pipes
